device.name: LED space Wi-Fi LED Screen (YSP-001 family)
device.notes: Wi-Fi sibling of the AUTOBABA LED Backpack on the same LOY SPACE / popled.cn platform — the third app binding documented for this protocol, alongside LOY SPACE (com.yskd.loywf) and NYAN GEAR (com.nyan.gear). Product listings name the panel YSP-001 (backpack screens, advertising vests, LED clothing); the same board family ships in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth variants, and the app drives both (FastBLE client plus a UDP path). The LED space app itself has been stale since 2023-06-29, but the platform ecosystem is active (LOY SPACE app updated 2026-03-25, backend CDNs live). Wi-Fi path: the device hosts a WPA/passphrase-protected AP whose SSID starts with "YS", secured with a well-known default password (12345678, per the app's own help text in 13 languages) that a user can change. The client joins it, broadcasts a TLV-serialized {"cmd":{"get":"dev_info"}} probe to 255.255.255.255:UDP/9090, and learns the device address from the reply sender (expected to be the ESP-style AP gateway 192.168.4.1 — not directly captured here). Commands are JSON objects app-side, serialized to binary 0xAA55-framed TLV on the wire by the native library libys_parse_tlv (parseJson/parseBin); replies come back as {"ack":{...},"sno":N}. Same wire frame as BLE: [0xAA, 0x55, 0xFF, 0xFF, len (u16-LE), sno (u16-LE), flags (0xC1), subflag, ...payload, checksum (u16-LE additive)] — over UDP each datagram chunk additionally carries an outer u16-LE length prefix (PacketDateUtils.toPacket), and large payloads are split into 180-byte chunks (writeFscNum; writeNum 120 on the other send path) with a ~5 ms inter-packet interval. Command vocabulary matches the AUTOBABA / NYAN specs (power, light 0-15, get dev_info/param_dev/param_wifi, delete del_all, rotate, pgm_play) and adds platform commands seen only in this app: dispatch, show_dev, pgm_flicker, bluetooth (radio control), timing (RTC set), delete del_ids, and a param_wifi SET command carrying user/pwd/ip_svr/port_svr/sec_hb — i.e. station-mode provisioning that points the panel at a server over a home network. Program upload uses the pkts_program JSON structure (60 sparse program slots, id_pro 11-19 seen in app templates) with zlib-compressed BMP pixel payloads (zip_bmp) built app-side by BmpUtils. Default screen geometry 64x64 (SharedPreferences default); 160x32 seen in UI code; dev_model default "gy", round panels detected by model containing "CXB5". CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the platform match — BLE UUIDs (fff0/fff1/fff2), JSON command strings, UDP port 9090 and popled.cn backend hosts (a.popled.cn, auth.popled.cn, wxbtapp.popled.cn:8443, app.popled.cn) verified in the vendor app; MEDIUM for Wi-Fi wire details — taken from the app's UDP/TLV code path, not replayed against hardware by this project.

credentials.notes: Anyone who joins the device AP can issue commands; the AP password (whose default is published in the vendor app's own help pages) is the only barrier.
stored_on_device: Optional station-mode credentials if param_wifi provisioning was used

factory_reset.effect: No account or owner binding exists to clear. The LOY SPACE platform command set includes {"cmd":{"delete":{"del_all":1}}} (clear all programs) and a format variant, which reset content, not credentials. If the AP password was changed from the default and lost, no software recovery path is documented — check the unit for a hardware reset button.

steps.action: Send the delete-all command over the joined AP.
steps.expect: All stored programs are erased; AP settings survive.

request.message: {"cmd":{"delete":{"del_all":1}},"ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N} to the device address on UDP 9090

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: The YS hotspot reappears and the device accepts commands again.

methods.description: The device itself is the AP — join it and speak the LOY SPACE TLV protocol over UDP port 9090. There is no account, no pairing PIN, and no credential exchange; physical proximity plus knowledge of the (default, documented-in-app) AP password is the only access control. Discovery: send the TLV serialization of {"cmd":{"get":"dev_info"}} broadcast to 255.255.255.255:9090; the device answers with {"ack":{"dev_info":{id_dev, model, version, cid, ...}},"sno":N} and subsequent commands go unicast to the reply address. The same discovery probe documented for the AUTOBABA backpack (aa 55 ff ff 08 00 01 00 c1 03 0a 00 d4 03) applies.

softap.ssid_notes: SSID starts with "YS"; default password 12345678 per the app's help text. gateway_ip is the expected ESP-style AP address — the app does not hardcode it; it broadcasts to 255.255.255.255:9090 and adopts the reply sender's address.

steps.action: Power the panel and join its Wi-Fi hotspot (SSID starts with YS, default password 12345678).
steps.expect: Client receives an address on the device AP network.
A reply datagram decoding to {"ack":{"dev_info":{...}},"sno":N}; adopt the sender address for unicast commands.

steps.action: Send commands unicast to the learned device address on UDP 9090.

setup.notes: AP-mode control needs no provisioning: the panel permanently hosts its own "YS…" Wi-Fi hotspot and accepts TLV/UDP commands from any client that joins it. The app's help flow is: join the YS hotspot with the default password 12345678, then the app broadcasts its dev_info probe and binds to the reply address. A station-mode provisioning command (param_wifi set with user/pwd/ip_svr/port_svr/sec_hb) exists in the app and can move the panel onto a home network pointed at a server, but it is not needed for local control and its post-provisioning behavior has not been captured.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the panel to an owner. Switching controllers is just joining the device AP from the new client and re-running discovery. Panels moved to a home network via the param_wifi provisioning command have not been observed and may need a unit-specific recovery path.

dispatch_program.description: Play one program for a fixed time. JSON: {"cmd":{"dispatch":{"type":1,"id_pro":N,"play_fixed_time":32767}},"ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N} (type 0 form carries a "value" key).

set_wifi_params.description: Station-mode provisioning: tells the panel to join a Wi-Fi network and contact a server. JSON: {"cmd":{"param_wifi":{"type":0,"user": "<ssid>","pwd":"<password>","ip_svr":"<server>","port_svr":"9090", "sec_hb":30}},"ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N}. Not needed for AP-mode local control; behavior after provisioning not captured.

show_dev.description: Device show flag, get and set. JSON: {"cmd":{"get":"show_dev"}} / {"cmd":{"show_dev":N},"ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N}

program_upload.description: Programs are built as a pkts_program JSON object — property_pro (width, height, gray, type_color, type_pro, play_loop), list_region with info_pos geometry, and list_item entries of type_item "text_pic" (text, color, size, font, alignment) or "graphic" (zip_bmp payload). App templates use id_pro 11-19; the platform supports 60 sparse program slots. In this app pgm_play carries the full ids_pro array (whole playlist); the sibling uni-app binding (autobaba-led-backpack.yaml) sends pgm_play with a single "index", and hardware-verified RE shows wire program-select is a single zero-based slot index — see the play_program command notes. zip_bmp is a zlib-compressed 24-bit BMP rendered app-side.

sequence.notes: The app keeps its sequence counter as the 32-bit value 4294901761 (0xFFFF0001) — stored as the string "4294901761" in Constant.sno and passed to the native TLV serializer as (int)4294901761L (Main2Activity.parseJson). Only the low 16 bits reach the wire: the frame's sno (u16-LE) is app_counter & 0xFFFF, so the first frame carries sno=1 (0xFFFF0001 & 0xFFFF = 1), matching the worked discovery frame above. The counter advances by one per command (Constant.getSnoLength = counter + 1) and the wire sno wraps every 65536. The app tracks reply sno values and accepts the next sequential one.

udp.discovery: TLV-serialized {"cmd":{"get":"dev_info"}} broadcast to 255.255.255.255:9090. The app learns the device address from the reply sender (as the app does) rather than hardcoding 192.168.4.1.
udp.framing: Each datagram chunk carries an outer u16-LE length prefix followed by that many bytes of 0xAA55-framed TLV payload (PacketDateUtils.toPacket). Large sends are split into 180-byte chunks (writeFscNum; 120 on the writeNum path) at ~5 ms intervals. Replies decode through the same TLV layer to JSON.
udp.retry: Vendor app: up to 10 resends at 8 s intervals until an ACK-shaped reply (matching sno) arrives; error replies are {"cmd":"err"} / {"cmd":"failed"}.

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: Notify characteristic (READ_ATTRIBUTE in the app's constants). Same semantics as the AUTOBABA spec: NOTIFY-only, enable the CCCD before writing or frames are not ACKed.

get_device_info.description: Query device info. JSON: {"cmd":{"get":"dev_info"}} (no ids_dev on the bare discovery probe)

play_program.description: Play programs. This com.yj.led (LED space) binding sends the whole playlist: {"cmd":{"pgm_play":{"model":0,"ids_pro":[1..60]}}, "ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N}, where ids_pro is the full 60-slot program-id array (the app's pgm_play template). The sibling uni-app binding documented in autobaba-led-backpack.yaml instead sends a single-slot form, {"cmd":{"pgm_play":{"model":0, "index":N}},...}; both are real JSON shapes for the same LOY SPACE pgm_play opcode across app versions. On the wire, hardware-verified RE (samrodrigues/loy-space-protocol) shows program selection is a single zero-based slot index, so a client that only needs to show one program can use the single-slot form. To play a single stored program this app also uses the dispatch command (dispatch_program above), not pgm_play.

power_toggle.description: Toggle screen power. JSON: {"cmd":{"power":{"type":0}},"ids_dev":"<id_dev>","sno":N} (this app also emits {"type":1}).

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: Write characteristic (WRITE_ATTRIBUTE in the app's constants). Same wire frame and checksum rules as the AUTOBABA spec; commands are the JSON vocabulary documented there and in popled_wifi_protocol above, serialized to binary TLV before send.
